releases.name: v0.2.3 — OpenCode 2.1.4 compatibility
releases.body:
# Azure DevOps PR Review for OpenCode — 0.2.3

This release moves the tested host to OpenCode CLI 2.1.4 and fixes three
behaviors that OpenCode 2.1.3 and later expose: how a refused proxy tunnel is
reported, how long a silent Azure DevOps call may wait, and how a refused
background summary affects a failed stage. Prompts, settings and installation
are unchanged.

## What changed

- **Proxy refusals are explained again.** OpenCode 2.1.3 and later embed Bun
  1.4.4, which rejects a request with `ERR_PROXY_TUNNEL` when a proxy refuses
  the CONNECT tunnel, where Bun 1.4.2 returned the proxy's answer. AZPR treated
  the rejection as a network error and retried it. It now gives the earlier
  messages and retry rules: a missing proxy password is explained as HTTP 407
  without retries, a blocked destination names the proxy, and a refused tunnel
  never leaves a comment write uncertain.
- **Azure DevOps calls keep their configured timeout.** The runtime's fetch
  ended a request that received nothing for about six minutes by itself, while
  `azure.callTimeoutSeconds` accepts up to 1,800 seconds. AZPR now switches that
  limit off for its requests, so the configured timeout decides.
- **Background compaction no longer splits a failed stage.** With OpenCode's
  opt-in `experimental.background_compaction`, the host asks for a summary
  before a reviewer's context is full. AZPR refuses it as before, but the
  refusal also marked the stage as overflowing: a later permanent failure,
  such as an expired provider key, split the shard into new sessions that
  failed the same way, and a failed follow-up discarded the answer it
  followed. Overflow is now read from the failed turn itself.
- The README states that AZPR is an independent community project, not built
  by or affiliated with the OpenCode team.

## Installation

```sh
opencode plugin add opencode-azure-devops-pr-review@0.2.3
```

Alternatively, install the same release from Git:

```sh
opencode plugin add 'github:WTLAIB/opencode-azure-devops-pr-review-v2#v0.2.3'
```

Add only one of them. Follow the
[quickstart](https://github.com/WTLAIB/opencode-azure-devops-pr-review-v2/blob/v0.2.3/docs/QUICKSTART.md)
for a private PAT file, `/pr-setup`, a service restart and the first review.

## Upgrading

Upgrade OpenCode to 2.1.4 first if you can: the receipts of other versions add
a host notice, and those versions are not validated. Stop the OpenCode service
and copy its database before upgrading OpenCode, so that you can go back.

To update a native installation, edit its existing entry in the OpenCode
configuration's `plugins` list:

- For npm, change the package specification to
  `opencode-azure-devops-pr-review@0.2.3`.
- For Git, change the tag suffix to `#v0.2.3`.

If the entry is an object, change only `package`; preserve `options.settingsFile`
and any other options. Keep one AZPR entry and restart the OpenCode service.
External settings, the PAT file and review records remain in place; a working
configuration needs no new `/pr-setup`. Exact version pins are not advanced by
`opencode plugin update`.

For a source installation, extract the new archive and run its installer with
`--replace` to retain settings:

```sh
sh install.sh --config-dir /absolute/path/to/v2-opencode-config --replace
```

Coming from 0.1.0, see the
[0.2.0 upgrade notes](https://github.com/WTLAIB/opencode-azure-devops-pr-review-v2/blob/v0.2.0/docs/releases/v0.2.0.md#upgrading-from-010)
for automatic comments, which remain disabled unless configured or requested.

## Compatibility and release assets

The tested target is OpenCode CLI **2.1.4** (V2 plugin API), Node.js
**22.23.3**, Ubuntu **22.04.5** under WSL2, and Azure DevOps Services REST API
**7.1**. OpenCode 1.x and Azure DevOps Server are not supported; other operating
systems remain unvalidated. See the
[validation record](https://github.com/WTLAIB/opencode-azure-devops-pr-review-v2/blob/v0.2.3/docs/VALIDATION.md),
including live reviews on OpenCode 2.1.4.

releases.name: v0.2.2 — Documentation and discovery metadata
releases.body:
# Azure DevOps PR Review for OpenCode — 0.2.2

This release brings the revised README and discovery metadata to npm. It
explains reviewing Azure DevOps PRs from a URL without maintaining a checkout,
model choices, separate verification, and comment previews. The runtime,
prompts, settings and installation behavior are unchanged from 0.2.1.

## What changed

- The README and quickstart share one first-review path:
  `/pr-review <PR URL> --preview`, with quick review as a lighter alternative.
- Compatibility explicitly excludes OpenCode 1.x. Detailed reference sections
  have visible navigation targets, and archive limits link to their actual guide.
- Azure Code Search is described as searching indexed branches; AZPR searches
  the selected commit snapshot. Model and performance claims stay within the
  documented evidence.
- The package has an updated description and the `opencode-v2` keyword.

## Installation

```sh
opencode plugin add opencode-azure-devops-pr-review@0.2.2
```

Alternatively, install the same release from Git:

```sh
opencode plugin add 'github:WTLAIB/opencode-azure-devops-pr-review-v2#v0.2.2'
```

Add only one of them. Follow the
[quickstart](https://github.com/WTLAIB/opencode-azure-devops-pr-review-v2/blob/v0.2.2/docs/QUICKSTART.md)
for a private PAT file, `/pr-setup`, a service restart and the first review.

## Upgrading

Existing 0.2.1 installations do not need an update to receive a runtime fix;
this is a documentation and metadata release. To update a native installation,
edit its existing entry in the OpenCode configuration's `plugins` list:

- For npm, change the package specification to
  `opencode-azure-devops-pr-review@0.2.2`.
- For Git, change the tag suffix to `#v0.2.2`.

If the entry is an object, change only `package`; preserve `options.settingsFile`
and any other options. Keep one AZPR entry and restart the OpenCode service.
External settings, the PAT file and review records remain in place; a working
configuration needs no new `/pr-setup`. Exact version pins are not advanced by
`opencode plugin update`.

For a source installation, extract the new archive and run its installer with
`--replace` to retain settings:

```sh
sh install.sh --config-dir /absolute/path/to/v2-opencode-config --replace
```

Coming from 0.1.0, see the
[0.2.0 upgrade notes](https://github.com/WTLAIB/opencode-azure-devops-pr-review-v2/blob/v0.2.0/docs/releases/v0.2.0.md#upgrading-from-010)
for automatic comments, which remain disabled unless configured or requested.

## Compatibility and release assets

The tested target remains OpenCode CLI **2.1.2** (V2 plugin API), Node.js
**22.23.3**, Ubuntu **22.04.5** under WSL2, and Azure DevOps Services REST API
**7.1**. OpenCode 1.x and Azure DevOps Server are not supported; other operating
systems remain unvalidated. See the
[validation record](https://github.com/WTLAIB/opencode-azure-devops-pr-review-v2/blob/v0.2.2/docs/VALIDATION.md).

The npm package comes from this tag and has no dependencies or install scripts.
Release assets are `opencode-azure-devops-pr-review-v2-0.2.2.tar.gz` and
`SHA256SUMS`; verify the source archive with `sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS`. The
existing demonstration remains attached to
[v0.2.0](https://github.com/WTLAIB/opencode-azure-devops-pr-review-v2/releases/tag/v0.2.0),
with its original recording context documented in the
[demo guide](https://github.com/WTLAIB/opencode-azure-devops-pr-review-v2/blob/v0.2.2/docs/DEMO.md).

releases.name: v0.2.1 — Install from npm
releases.body:
# OpenCode Azure DevOps PR Review V2 — 0.2.1

AZPR is now available from the npm registry. This release changes packaging
and documentation only: the runtime, prompts and settings are the same as in
0.2.0.

## Installation

```sh
opencode plugin add opencode-azure-devops-pr-review@0.2.1
```

The same release remains available as a versioned Git package, which needs
Git but not the npm registry:

```sh
opencode plugin add 'github:WTLAIB/opencode-azure-devops-pr-review-v2#v0.2.1'
```

Add only one of them. Follow the [quickstart](https://github.com/WTLAIB/opencode-azure-devops-pr-review-v2/blob/v0.2.1/docs/QUICKSTART.md)
for `/pr-setup`, a private PAT file, service restart and your first review.
The source archive includes `install.sh` for manual installation. Use one
installation method per OpenCode profile.

## Upgrading

For a native installation, edit the existing AZPR entry in the OpenCode
configuration's `plugins` list:

- To stay on Git, change `#v0.2.0` (or `#v0.1.0`) to `#v0.2.1`.
- To move to npm, replace the Git specification with
  `opencode-azure-devops-pr-review@0.2.1`.

If the entry is an object, change only its `package` value; preserve
`options.settingsFile` and other options. Keep one AZPR entry, then restart the
OpenCode service. npm and Git installations read the same external settings, so
the settings, PAT file and review records stay in place and a working
configuration needs no new `/pr-setup`. Exact versions stay pinned:
`opencode plugin update` leaves them unchanged, so change the version yourself
for later releases.

Coming from 0.1.0, you also gain automatic comments, which stay disabled until
you configure them; see the
[0.2.0 notes](https://github.com/WTLAIB/opencode-azure-devops-pr-review-v2/blob/v0.2.0/docs/releases/v0.2.0.md#upgrading-from-010).

For a source installation, extract the new archive and run its installer with
`--replace`. Only documentation differs from 0.2.0 there, so this is optional.

```sh
sh install.sh --config-dir /absolute/path/to/v2-opencode-config --replace
```

## Compatibility and release assets

The tested target remains OpenCode CLI **2.1.2**, Node.js **22.23.3**, Ubuntu
**22.04.5** under WSL2, and Azure DevOps Services REST API **7.1**.
[Validation](https://github.com/WTLAIB/opencode-azure-devops-pr-review-v2/blob/v0.2.1/docs/VALIDATION.md)
records the release checks. Azure DevOps Server and other operating systems
remain unvalidated.

The npm package is built from this tag with `npm pack` and has no
dependencies or install scripts. Release assets are the source archive
`opencode-azure-devops-pr-review-v2-0.2.1.tar.gz` and `SHA256SUMS`; verify
downloads with `sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS`. The demonstration video stays
attached to [v0.2.0](https://github.com/WTLAIB/opencode-azure-devops-pr-review-v2/releases/tag/v0.2.0).

releases.name: v0.2.0 — Opt-in comments after review
releases.body:
# OpenCode Azure DevOps PR Review V2 — 0.2.0

A completed review can now preview or publish its comments automatically,
without another `/pr-comment` command. This is opt-in: existing installations
keep the manual workflow until you select a setting or command flag.

## What changed

- `afterReview` selects `none`, `preview` or `publish` separately for `quick`,
  `review` and `deep`. Every mode defaults to `none`.
- One flag immediately after the PR URL (`--preview`, `--publish` or
  `--no-comment`) overrides that setting for a single review. Mistyped flags
  there produce an error; they do not fall back to automatic publication.
- A COMPLETE review starts the comment step as its own run, with a STARTED
  notice and receipt. `/pr-stop` cancels it. A stopped review starts no step;
  a review without findings needs no extra planning or model request. A busy
  conversation or PR skips the step and gives the command to run manually.
- Automatic publication holds individual items containing mentions, images,
  active HTML or script/private-file links in the saved preview. Other items
  are posted and read back. Ordinary links and unambiguous literal code are
  allowed; mentions are checked in code too. Inspect held items before using
  the explicit `/pr-comment <review-id> --publish` command.
- When every finding is already discussed on the PR, automatic publication
  reports `NOTHING_TO_POST` instead of adding another summary.
- Quick comments keep their "not independently verified" disclosure;
  severity and incomplete coverage do not block the whole publication.
- `/pr-check` shows the configured automatic action and posting identity as
  information. Setup errors identify the settings problem without values.
- The automatic-publication HTML checks read long tag-like text in linear
  time, avoiding the slowdown found during review of this feature.

For a one-off preview, substitute your own authorized Azure PR URL:

```text
/pr-review https://dev.azure.com/YOUR_ORGANIZATION/YOUR_PROJECT/_git/YOUR_REPO/pullrequest/123 --preview
```

Use `--publish` in the same position to request automatic publication, or
`--no-comment` to suppress a configured automatic action for that run.
To default to previews, add this to AZPR's settings and restart the service:

```json
{
  "afterReview": {
    "quick": "preview",
    "review": "preview",
    "deep": "preview"
  }
}
```

See [automatic comments](https://github.com/WTLAIB/opencode-azure-devops-pr-review-v2/blob/v0.2.0/docs/COMMENTING.md#automatic-comments-after-a-review)
for the per-item checks, cancellation and publication receipts. Review prompts
and the verified versus quick review methods are unchanged.

## Installation

```sh
opencode plugin add 'github:WTLAIB/opencode-azure-devops-pr-review-v2#v0.2.0'
```

Follow the [quickstart](https://github.com/WTLAIB/opencode-azure-devops-pr-review-v2/blob/v0.2.0/docs/QUICKSTART.md)
for `/pr-setup`, a private PAT file, service restart and your first review.
The source archive includes `install.sh` for manual installation. Use one
installation method per OpenCode profile. This is a Git package release; it
does not publish an npm registry package.

## Upgrading from 0.1.0

For a native installation, edit the existing AZPR entry in the OpenCode
configuration's `plugins` list: change
`github:WTLAIB/opencode-azure-devops-pr-review-v2#v0.1.0` to
`github:WTLAIB/opencode-azure-devops-pr-review-v2#v0.2.0`. If the entry is an
object, change only its `package` value; preserve `options.settingsFile` and
other options. Keep one AZPR entry, then restart the OpenCode service. Native
settings remain outside the package cache, and missing `afterReview` values
default to `none`.

For a source installation, extract the new archive and run its installer:

```sh
sh install.sh --config-dir /absolute/path/to/v2-opencode-config --replace
```

This preserves operational settings and adds missing defaults. Keep the PAT
file and private state directory in place. Neither ins

releases.name: AZPR v0.1.0
releases.body:
# OpenCode Azure DevOps PR Review V2 — 0.1.0

Review Azure DevOps pull requests in OpenCode, preview the resulting comments,
and choose when to publish them.

## Included

- `/pr-setup`: configure your organization, one model and an existing private
  PAT file. Settings stay outside a native package's cache and survive updates.
- `/pr-check`: check Azure access, source reads and model readiness without
  calling a model.
- `/pr-quick`: one reviewer per shard covers function and risk. Findings are
  reported, not independently verified.
- `/pr-review` and `/pr-deep`: separate functional and risk reviews, followed
  by independent verification sessions. `/pr-deep` runs the same review with
  the stronger models configured in `models.deep`.
- `/pr-comment`: preview the summary and inline comments. Add `--publish` to
  post the saved plan; publication checks the PR head, skips existing markers
  and reads posted comments back.
- `/pr-stop`: cancel the active command in your conversation.
- Large-PR sharding, overflow recovery, bounded retries and two concurrent
  comment-planning pages.
- Private saved reviews and publication records, and Azure proxy/CA settings.
- The PAT kept alone in an owner-only file (`azure.patFile`), so
  `settings.json` holds no secret.

## Installation

Install with OpenCode V2's plugin manager:

```sh
opencode plugin add 'github:WTLAIB/opencode-azure-devops-pr-review-v2#v0.1.0'
```

Follow [the quickstart](https://github.com/WTLAIB/opencode-azure-devops-pr-review-v2/blob/v0.1.0/docs/QUICKSTART.md)
to create a private PAT file, run `/pr-setup` with one model and your Azure
organization, then restart the OpenCode service. Review, preview and publication
are separate explicit commands.

The source archive also includes `install.sh` for manual installation into the
configuration directory used by your OpenCode V2 instance.

For an existing AZPR V2 installation, use the documented `--replace` option;
it preserves settings and adds defaults. Do not enable both installation methods
in one profile. This release does not require an npm registry package.

## Compatibility and evidence

- Tested host: `@opencode/cli` **2.1.2**.
- Tested OS: **Ubuntu 22.04**; the recorded environment uses WSL2.
- Azure: **Azure DevOps Services**, REST API **7.1**.
- Native installer: OpenCode's Git package manager. Alternative source installer:
  POSIX `sh` and Python 3 standard library. No plugin build step or npm dependencies.

`docs/VALIDATION.md` records the offline tests, real-host tests with fake
services, and separate live Azure/model runs. Model quality and runtime
correctness are different claims; test counts do not establish review accuracy.

The release includes a real OpenCode terminal demonstration and Azure comment
read-back recording; see the [demo guide](https://github.com/WTLAIB/opencode-azure-devops-pr-review-v2/blob/v0.1.0/docs/DEMO.md)
for the source, environment, edits and limitations.

## Before using it with a team

Read `docs/ENTERPRISE.md` for data sent to the selected model, PAT permissions,
private retention, network configuration and publication behavior.

Quick findings are not independently verified. Preview generation uses a model
and can incur cost. A session can make multiple model requests; no fixed cost
or accuracy is promised. Azure DevOps Server is not supported; operating
systems other than the tested Linux environment remain unvalidated. The minimum
recommended PAT scopes and quick-review publication have been confirmed on the
dedicated Azure test repository; other organizations and repositories still need
their own acceptance checks.
